findings.analysis: MS05 unqualified wording extends the new selected-product obligation to acquisition failures before its target is knowable. A syntactically valid manifest larger than 16MiB, padded with inactive JSON and containing an exact product-alias export, cannot both be refused before allocation and have its selected target established. Likewise a metadata budget can end before the deciding manifest. The surrounding known-negative language suggests the intended bounded interpretation but does not explicitly limit the mandatory acceptance. This is a documentary executability/precedence ambiguity, not a demonstrated implementation regression or false proof.
findings.minimalRemedy: State explicitly: retain and prioritize every violation already discovered, including across subsequent errors/caps; run the existing bounded negative census before semantic/refinement caps at its defined stages; require new selected-product VIOLATION when the deciding metadata and link chain were acquired within the existing bounds. If acquisition/deadline fails before the target is known, return explicit UNKNOWN with zero proofs, retaining all prior violations, without bypassing caps. Add paired MS05/MS07 controls: target known then reduced semantic/workspace cap => VIOLATION; metadata acquisition cap before target known => UNKNOWN/no proof/no lost earlier violation. Do not weaken the existing full-v2 multiset retention requirement.
